bands.label: Strong
bands.blurb: Solid contracts, transparent operations, and an easy start.

providers.name: Knownwell
providers.description: Knownwell is an AI-powered commercial intelligence platform for B2B professional services firms, built around client retention and expansion rather than new-logo acquisition. The platform ingests communications, CRM records, and enterprise data through connectors to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Teams, and conversation intelligence tools, then synthesizes an objective Knownwell score for every client relationship. Teams use it to detect churn risk before a renewal conversation, surface growth opportunities across a portfolio, and track relationship health over time without manual data entry. Knownwell publishes a read-only public REST API at api.knownwell.com/ci/v1 that exposes client scores, score history, portfolios, streams, topics, priorities, notes, key people, and the weekly Red/Amber/Green alignment reads a client team files by hand, authenticated with an X-API-Key header. Platform pricing is published as a live per-client volume calculator rather than named tiers, with a 30-day trial and no per-seat charge. Knownwell was acquired by 2X to form a human-agentic GTM services company.

bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: Hubflo
providers.description: Hubflo is a client portal platform for service businesses — consultants, agencies, accountants, and professional-service firms — bringing client onboarding, messaging, document management, e-signatures, forms, proposals, invoicing, tasks, and project collaboration into one branded workspace. Hubflo exposes a REST API (v2) at app.hubflo.com/api/v2 with bearer-token authentication, JSON request/response bodies, UUID resource identifiers, page-based pagination, a 1000 request/minute rate limit, and a native webhook system spanning 29 event types across companies, contacts, workspaces, invoices, forms, tasks, and e-signature submissions. Hubflo also publishes official TypeScript and MCP-server packages and a hosted remote MCP server. Backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Coordinate
providers.description: Coordinate (CoordinateHQ) is a client project-execution platform and branded client portal for client-facing businesses — agencies, professional services, and B2B onboarding teams. It turns repeatable workflows into automated, interactive projects with tasks, task groups, goals, progress reports, forms, eSignatures, time tracking, and in-project chat, while giving each client a simple password-free portal. Coordinate exposes a REST API (base https://app.coordinatehq.com/api/v1) for creating and syncing projects, tasks, groups, stakeholders, goals, comments, and organizations, an /entity export firehose for bulk sync, and a webhook API for real-time create/update events, alongside bi-directional Zapier integrations. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Coordinate's published API reference.

providers.name: Laurel
providers.description: Laurel is an AI timekeeping and work-intelligence platform for professional services firms — law, accounting and advisory. Rather than asking timekeepers to record their own time, Laurel passively captures work activity across the applications people already work in, then uses machine learning to enrich each activity with the who, what, when, where and how needed to build a review-ready timesheet. Reviewed time is released into the firm's existing billing or practice-management system, and Laurel's Signal product layers operational and profitability analytics on top of the resulting time data. Laurel exposes three public APIs — Identity, Time and Ingestion — authenticated with OAuth 2.0 machine-to-machine client credentials, and documents them at developer.laurel.ai for firms and partners building connectors.

providers.name: legal.ge Public APIs
providers.description: Georgia's (the country's) legal marketplace, exposing a public, keyless, read-only REST API that turns a natural-language description of a legal problem into matched practice areas and a ranked list of verified specialists — lawyers, law firms, accountants, tax consultants, mediators and enforcement agents — each with a canonical, locale-prefixed profile URL. The surface is deliberately agent-first: an OpenAPI 3.1 contract at /api/openapi.json, an APIs.json 0.19 index at /apis.json, an llms.txt trust contract at /llms.txt, a robots.txt that names and allows eleven AI crawlers on the public API paths, and an installable MCP server (@legalge/mcp, MIT) exposing find_legal_specialists and classify_legal_intent to Claude Desktop, Cursor and any MCP-aware client. Trilingual across Georgian, English and Russian; every specialist returned is verification-checked, and contact details are opt-in only.

providers.name: KPMG
providers.description: KPMG is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating through a global network of independent member firms affiliated with KPMG International Limited, a private English company limited by guarantee that itself does not provide services to clients. The network spans more than 276,000 partners and employees across 138 countries and territories. KPMG organizes delivery across six service lines — Audit & Assurance, Tax, Legal, Advisory, ESG, and AI — and serves six industries: Consumer / Retail / Leisure; Energy, Natural Resources & Chemicals; Financial Services; Healthcare; Government & Public Sector; and Private Enterprise. AI is a first-class service line built on the KPMG Trusted AI framework — a ten-pillar approach covering Reliability, Security, Safety, Privacy, Sustainability, Explainability, Integrity, Transparency, Fairness, and Accountability — and packaged through five AI solutions: KPMG AI Jumpstart, AI Strategy, AI Trust, AI Workforce, and AI Technology. Alliances anchoring the AI delivery surface include Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, and Workday, with collaboration noted with the World Economic Forum. KPMG Lakehouse, the firm's USD 450 million learning-and-innovation campus in Lake Nona, Orlando, is the cultural and AI-upskilling hub for the US firm and a venue for client innovation sessions in generative AI, ESG, and talent strategy. Insights is KPMG's research-publishing surface, organized across topic categories including AI and Technology, ESG, Operations, Risk and Regulation, Transformation, Value Creation, Workforce, Public Policy & Regulatory Change, Business Transformation, Audit & Assurance, Tax, Advisory, Sustainability, and Transactions, with flagship series such as the KPMG US Technology Survey Report, the KPMG Global Third-Party Risk Management Survey, the KPMG M&A Deal Market Study, Fit for Pillar Two, and AI Governance Principles for Boards. KPMG does not publish a public developer API or corporate developer portal at the network level; the firm has no enumerable public GitHub organization at `github.com/kpmg`. The one meaningful public API surface inside the KPMG brand is KPMG Origins (`kpmgorigins.com`) — an Australian regulated-waste tracking platform (initially the NSW Integrated Waste Tracking System / IWTS, with Queensland and other jurisdictions in scope) that exposes two REST APIs (Movements + Registries) over Swagger with API-key authentication, intended for integration with waste-operator software rather than as a general-purpose KPMG developer surface. Distribution to readers and client stakeholders flows through the Insights site, the US Subscription Center (Opportunity (In)sight monthly newsletter), KPMG Australia's Business Insights podcast, and per-page RSS feeds offered on individual KPMG member-firm pages.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Mosaic
providers.description: Mosaic is a resource management, workforce planning, and AI-assisted project management platform built for architecture, engineering, and professional services firms. It plugs into the ERPs those firms already run — Deltek (Ajera, Vantagepoint, Vision, Costpoint), Unanet, BST10, BQE Core, QuickBooks, Salesforce, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 — plus project management systems (Asana, Jira, GitHub, Karbon) and HRIS (BambooHR), then unifies the data into a single forecasting, time-entry, and capacity-planning surface. Mosaic exposes an Open API for custom integrations alongside its packaged connectors.

providers.name: Vistra
providers.description: Vistra is a global corporate services provider operating in over 45 jurisdictions, offering entity management, incorporation, compliance, payroll, and fund administration services. The Vistra REST API enables developers to programmatically submit company incorporation requests in supported jurisdictions (initially British Virgin Islands), upload supporting documents to pre-signed storage URLs, and integrate Vistra's corporate services into business process workflows. Authentication uses OAuth2 bearer tokens obtained through the Vistra Developer Portal.

providers.name: Harvest
providers.description: Harvest is a cloud-based time tracking, project management, expense tracking, and invoicing platform used by agencies, consultancies, and professional services teams to track billable hours, manage budgets, and bill clients. The platform provides reporting on team utilization, project profitability, and budget burn, and integrates with tools like Asana, Trello, Slack, and QuickBooks. Harvest's REST API v2 provides full programmatic access to clients, projects, tasks, time entries, expenses, invoices, estimates, and users using OAuth 2.0 or Personal Access Token authentication.

providers.name: Advantage Solutions
providers.description: Advantage Solutions is a leading provider of outsourced sales, marketing, merchandising, and business intelligence services to consumer goods manufacturers and retailers across North America. The company supports brand growth through retail execution, in-store demos, digital commerce enablement, and shopper insights, and publishes Advantage360 shopper and market research alongside the MRKT industry publication. Advantage Solutions does not operate a developer program, publish API documentation, or offer a commercial API product. The only machine-readable surface it serves is the standard WordPress REST API of its corporate site (youradv.com) and of MRKT (mrktblog.com), both of which return published content anonymously.

providers.name: CBRE
providers.description: CBRE Group, Inc. (NYSE: CBRE) is the world's largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with 155,000 professionals across 500+ offices in 100+ countries. CBRE provides advisory and transaction, project management, property management, valuation, investment management, and consulting services. Its technology arm publishes developer APIs through developer.cbre.com that expose property, analytics, and facilities data to partners.

providers.name: McKinsey & Company
providers.description: McKinsey & Company is the senior partner of the MBB triumvirate of global strategy and management consulting firms, founded in 1926 by James O. McKinsey and headquartered in New York City. The firm operates from 130-plus cities across more than 65 countries with roughly 38,000-45,000 people serving corporations, governments, and not-for-profit organizations. McKinsey delivers through industry practices and cross-cutting capability practices: Strategy & Corporate Finance, Operations, Marketing & Sales, Risk & Resilience, Sustainability, Transformation, Implementation, Organization (formerly OrgSolutions), Growth / Marketing / Sales, McKinsey Digital, and McKinsey Technology. McKinsey Digital houses QuantumBlack (the AI division acquired in 2015), Leap (venture / business building), and the Technology practice. Internal generative-AI tooling is consolidated in Lilli, a McKinsey-built consultant assistant launched in August 2023 that indexes 100,000+ internal documents and is used by tens of thousands of firm employees. Research and thought leadership are published through McKinsey Insights, McKinsey Quarterly (the firm's flagship business journal since 1964), McKinsey Global Institute (MGI, the firm's business and economics research arm), the QuantumBlack AI report and State of AI survey, industry-specific reports, podcasts (The McKinsey Podcast, McKinsey Talks Operations, etc.), and the McKinsey on Books series. McKinsey does not publish a public commercial developer API or developer portal; all software the firm releases publicly flows through GitHub. The official `github.com/mckinsey` organization hosts a focused open-source portfolio centered on data, AI, and agentic systems — Vizro (low-code Plotly/Dash data-visualization toolkit), Agents-at-Scale ARK (Kubernetes-native framework for portable agentic applications), Agents-at-Scale Marketplace (curated Helm-chart catalog of ARK executors, MCP servers, and tools), CausalNex (Bayesian-network causal-reasoning library), QuantumBlack Design System (shadcn-based React component registry), and qbstyles (QuantumBlack Matplotlib themes). Kedro, the production-grade data and ML pipeline framework originally built inside QuantumBlack, was donated to the Linux Foundation (LF AI & Data) and is now governed at `github.com/kedro-org`.

providers.name: COR
providers.description: COR (COR Global Ltd., projectcor.com) is an AI-powered management platform for advertising and creative agencies that calculates and forecasts project profitability while managing finances, resources, projects, tasks, and time tracking in one real-time workspace. COR publishes a REST API (JSON or XML) for projects, tasks, hours, clients, contracts, transactions, teams, users, and more, a separate Resource Allocation API, and an official hosted MCP server so AI clients can operate a workspace with natural language. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Memory
providers.description: Memory AS (operating as Timely, timely.com) is an Oslo, Norway based software company behind Timely, an AI-powered automatic time tracking and timesheet platform for consultancies, agencies, professional-services firms and SaaS teams. Its Memory tracking engine passively captures work across the apps a person uses and its AutoSheet feature auto-completes timesheets, letting teams auto-capture, auto-allocate and one-click approve time. Timely exposes a REST API at api.timelyapp.com (version 1.1) secured with OAuth 2.0 for building on accounts, projects, clients, users, events (time entries) and reports, and offers 90+ direct integrations with tools such as QuickBooks, Xero, Asana, Jira, GitHub, Slack, Google Calendar and Salesforce. The company is ISO 27001:2022 certified and GDPR-aligned, backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Ernst & Young (EY)
providers.description: Ernst & Young (EY) is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating as a global network of member firms branded under "EY" and coordinated by Ernst & Young Global Limited (EYG). EY reports a workforce of roughly 400,000 people spanning approximately 150 countries. The firm's stated purpose is "Building a better working world" and it organizes delivery across a small set of professional service lines — Assurance, Consulting, Strategy & Transactions (branded as EY-Parthenon, covering both Strategy and Transactions and Corporate Finance), Tax, Law, Technology, Managed Services, and People & Workforce Services — plus EY Private (services for privately-held and entrepreneur-led businesses) and EY Sustainability. Industry coverage is organized into eight sectors: Industrials & Mobility, Consumer Products & Retail, Energy & Resources, Financial Services, Government & Infrastructure, Health & Life Sciences, Private Equity, and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. EY's flagship technology initiative is EY.ai, positioned as an enterprise-scale "agentic AI unifying platform" backed by alliances with NVIDIA, Microsoft, IBM, SAP, ServiceNow and others. Adjacent platform brands include EY Nexus (a sector-tailored business transformation platform marketed primarily to financial services), EY Studio+ (customer experience / growth), EY Ecosystems (partnership network), and EY wavespace (innovation centers). EY's research-publishing surface is the EY Insights portfolio, organized around topic areas (AI, Finance, Geostrategy, People and Workforce, Risk, Sustainability, Technology, EY Transformation) and flagship recurring series including the CEO Outlook, EY Megatrends, Global IPO Trends, the Private Equity Pulse, Work Reimagined, the Climate Action Barometer, and the Nature Action Barometer, plus EY Podcasts and EY Webcasts. Project Everest — the proposed split of EY's audit and consulting businesses — was publicly cancelled in April 2023, and EY continues to operate as an integrated multi-line professional services organization. EY does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, public REST APIs, or a consumer-facing API pricing surface at the global corporate level. The only first-party EY GitHub organization that is publicly discoverable is EYBlockchain (github.com/EYBlockchain, ~28 public repositories, ~160 followers, blog URL blockchain.ey.com), which hosts EY's open-source zero-knowledge cryptography and privacy-preserving blockchain work, anchored by the Nightfall optimistic-rollup family (Nightfall_3 in JavaScript / Nightfall_4 Community Edition in Rust) and the Starlight Solidity-to-zApp transpiler, alongside supporting libraries such as Timber, Poseidon, halo2-lib, snark-verifier, plonkish, algebra, and ZoKrates wrappers, plus product brands EY Blockchain Analyzer (Reconciler and Smart Contract & Token Review) and the EY OpsChain Suite (Traceability, ESG, Contract Manager).

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: Deloitte
providers.description: Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating through a network of member firms coordinated by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited (DTTL). The organization spans approximately 150 countries and territories, has more than 180 years of history (founded 1845), and serves roughly 90% of the Fortune Global 500. Deloitte organizes delivery across four primary service lines — Audit & Assurance, Consulting, Tax, and Legal — plus specialized cross-functional practices including Business Process Solutions and Global Employer Services. Consulting offerings cover Customer, Cyber, Engineering / AI & Data, Enterprise Technology & Performance, Finance Transformation, Human Capital, Strategy & Transactions, and Risk / Regulatory & Forensic. Deloitte Digital is the technology-and-experience practice with alliances spanning Salesforce, Adobe, SAP, Google Cloud, AWS, ServiceNow, Oracle, Shopify, Sitecore, and Genesys, and accelerators such as FrontOffice Advantage, Revenue Advantage, Agentic Marketing Cloud, CreativEdge, Blueprint, Content Studios, and TrustID. The organization serves six industries divided into twenty sectors: Consumer; Energy, Resources & Industrials; Financial Services; Government & Public Services; Life Sciences & Health Care; and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. Deloitte Insights is the organization's research-publishing surface, organized into eight research centers — Cross-Industry, Economics, Consumer, Energy & Industrials, Financial Services, Government & Public Services, Life Sciences & Health Care, and Tech, Media & Telecom — producing flagship series including Tech Trends, Global Human Capital Trends, Digital Media Trends, TMT Predictions, FSI Predictions, the Weekly Global Economic Outlook, and the annual Industry Outlooks. The Deloitte AI Institute drives applied-AI research and points of view. Deloitte does not publish a public developer API or open developer portal at the corporate level. The Deloitte US Consulting GitHub organization is small (5 visible repositories, mostly archived upstream forks; the original artifact is `beacon`, a first-party web-analytics packaging library in TypeScript). Reader-facing distribution flows through MyDeloitte (personalized content + newsletter subscriptions), Dbriefs (live webcasts with CPE credit), the Deloitte Insights Magazine, and the YouTube channel; no public RSS index page was discoverable on www.deloitte.com at the path published in legacy archives.

providers.name: Linguidoor
providers.description: Linguidoor is a Berlin-based, ISO-branded human translation and localization agency serving businesses and individuals across Germany and internationally. It offers professional translation in 100+ languages, website / app / software / game localization, MTPE, certified and sworn document translation for German administrative processes (birth and marriage certificates, driving licences, Anmeldung, Schufa, diplomas), interpretation, subtitling and captioning, voice-over and dubbing, transcription, desktop publishing, content writing, international SEO, and AI data services (data annotation, tagging and labeling, voice and text data collection, text-to-speech and voice cloning). Pricing is published per translated word across three service tiers, with fixed-price certified document translations sold through an online shop. Linguidoor publishes NO developer program: enrichment found no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP server, agent card, SDK, CLI or API documentation of any kind. The site is WordPress + WooCommerce on Hostinger; its only machine-readable surfaces are the platform-default WordPress REST API at /wp-json/ (which includes the public unauthenticated WooCommerce Store API) and a plugin-generated llms.txt whose entire content is the default WordPress "Hello world!" post.

providers.name: Introhive
providers.description: Introhive is a relationship intelligence and CRM data automation platform used primarily by professional services firms — law, accounting, consulting and the built environment — to remove manual CRM data entry. It passively mines employee email and calendar systems to build a firm-wide relationship graph of who knows whom and how strong each relationship is, then cleans, de-duplicates and enriches contact, company and activity records before writing them back into the system of record. Introhive integrates with Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot and legal/accounting practice systems, and surfaces the resulting intelligence through a relationship portal, digest emails and CRM-embedded apps. The company is headquartered in Fredericton, New Brunswick, Canada, and operates regional platform instances for the US, Canada and the UK.

providers.name: Intellectible
providers.description: Intellectible is an AI build platform for enterprise service providers - federal and state government contractors (GovCon), professional services firms, and economic development organizations - that turns portals, emails, CRM data, and market signals into structured opportunity, proposal, pricing, and knowledge workflows. Its horizontal build environment (project workspaces, visual workflows, document libraries, PostgreSQL databases, applications, pages, jobs, and queues) is exposed programmatically through the Intellectible Public API and a Code Execution SDK, letting teams run workflows synchronously, manage Library files, and query project databases directly from code.

providers.name: Halborn
providers.description: Halborn is a blockchain and digital-asset cybersecurity firm that sells professional security services rather than a developer product. Its assurance practice covers smart contract assessments, Layer 1 protocol reviews, code security audits, web application and cloud infrastructure penetration testing, red team exercises, and custody and key management assessments; its advisory practice covers AI security, blockchain architecture, compliance readiness, risk assessment, technical due diligence and technical training for banks, exchanges, custodians, tokenization platforms, stablecoin issuers, DeFi protocols, central banks and blockchain infrastructure providers. Halborn publishes its engagement results as a public audit repository, discloses zero-day findings under its own CVE assignment scope as a CVE Numbering Authority, and maintains BVSS, the Blockchain Vulnerability Scoring System. As of August 2026 it publishes no public API, no developer portal and no machine-readable contract; its Halborn ONE client platform at one.halborn.com is an invitation-only customer portal.

providers.name: Blue J
providers.description: Blue J is an AI-powered tax research platform that delivers defensible, source-backed answers to complex tax questions in seconds, drawing on primary law plus Tax Notes and IBFD content. Built for tax professionals, the platform supports advisory, compliance, tax writing, and training workflows, and is trusted by 4,000+ firms including Crowe, RSM, and Larson. Blue J is a SaaS product accessed through its web application at app.askbluej.com; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or MCP server. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Sapphire Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Blue J's own public website, security, pricing, and trust-center pages.

providers.name: Vesence
providers.description: Vesence builds agentic AI for professional-services firms that works directly inside Microsoft Office. Its agents operate in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, plus a web app, reviewing emails, documents and projects before they leave the firm and turning Microsoft Word into a purpose-built workspace for high-stakes drafting, quality assurance and knowledge work. Vesence connects to SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Teams and document-management systems so agents work with a firm's existing files and context, with every edit traceable through tracked changes. Trusted by law firms, banks and investors, Vesence targets transactional legal work such as fund formation, M&A and corporate matters. It is a Y Combinator-backed startup surfaced through the venture portfolios of Creandum and Emergence Capital.

providers.name: Provus
providers.description: Provus (Provusinc) is an agentic AI Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ) platform built specifically for services organizations — professional services, consulting, and asset-based services firms. The platform turns unstructured inputs such as emails, RFPs, and call notes into structured, accurate services quotes, and runs a set of AI agents (Quote Optimizer, Deal Predictor, Proposal Response, Deal Rescue, and Provus Admin) that monitor deals, optimize pricing, assess risk, and protect margin. Provus ships two products — CPQ Express for growing teams and Enterprise Services CPQ for large organizations — with native connectors to Salesforce, HubSpot, Kantata, NetSuite, and DocuSign. It is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and reports managing over $5B in enterprise services revenue across customers including Thoughtworks, Trace3, and Prolifics. Provus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; integration is delivered through native prebuilt connectors and a Salesforce AppExchange managed package, and product help documentation is hosted on a Document360 knowledge base at docs.provus.ai that 302s the entire site to a login. Provus names an internal "Profet API" in its published sub-processor list, but that service is not documented, versioned, or reachable publicly.

providers.name: Accordance Ai
providers.description: Accordance (operated by Agnetic Labs Inc.) is a San Francisco frontier AI platform built for tax, audit, and accounting professionals. Founded by researchers from the Stanford AI Lab, it provides a firmwide agentic AI platform that performs tax research with authoritative code, context, and citations, complex accounting analysis, and audit insight — with visible reasoning and verifiable source citations. Accordance is SOC 2 Type II certified, never trains on customer data, and is backed by Menlo Ventures, Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and New Enterprise Associates. The product surface is the Accordance application (app.accordance.ai); no public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Accenture
providers.description: A global professional services company providing consulting, technology, and outsourcing services. Serves clients across more than 40 industries in over 120 countries with expertise in digital transformation, cloud, and AI.

providers.name: LegalOS
providers.description: LegalOS is an AI-native U.S. immigration law practice based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Founded by Matthew Asir (CEO), Rachel Asir (COO) and Claire Jutabha (CTO), the company pairs proprietary legal software with licensed immigration attorneys to prepare employment-based visa and green-card petitions — H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, O-1 and TN visas, plus EB-1A, EB-1C and EB-2 NIW green cards. AI agents draft petition narratives, assemble supporting evidence and anticipate USCIS objections, with every filing reviewed by a licensed attorney before submission. LegalOS is delivered as a service through a customer web application at app.legalos.ai; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: HubSync
providers.description: HubSync is an AI-powered, end-to-end tax and accounting workflow platform built for CPA firms, founded in 2019 by John McGowan and headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee. The SaaS platform unifies the engagement lifecycle in one interface: engagement letter generation and tracking, tax organizers and prepared-by-client data collection, document management, e-signature (including IRS Form 8879), batch federal and state extensions, tax return breakup and delivery, e-file status tracking, web-based tax workpapers, firm analytics dashboards, and integrated bill-and-pay. Its HubSync Halo layer adds agentic AI orchestration across those stages. HubSync publishes an llms.txt and states that it ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and bi-directional API integrations with CCH Axcess/ProSystem fx, Thomson Reuters GoSystem/UltraTax and SurePrep, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI description or endpoint documentation — the entire integration surface is provisioned per customer firm.

providers.name: Gartner
providers.description: Gartner is a global research and advisory firm providing information, advice, and tools to business leaders across IT, finance, HR, customer service, sales, marketing, supply chain, and legal functions. Gartner does not publish a public developer API; this repository tracks the company and any partner or technical artifacts that surface over time.

providers.name: Paro
providers.description: Paro is an AI-powered professional services marketplace that connects businesses and accounting firms with vetted, on-demand finance and accounting experts. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Chicago, Paro uses proprietary AI matching to pair clients with the top 2% of finance professionals across 60+ industries and 250+ skill sets — spanning bookkeeping, fractional CFO and controller services, financial planning and analysis, tax and compliance, and full-time recruiting. For accounting firms it provides staff augmentation, busy-season support, and service-expansion consulting. Paro operates a talent platform (app.paro.io) but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, content, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Harness Wealth
providers.description: Harness — the company that launched as Harness Wealth, and today a wholly owned business of Multiplier, Inc. — is a New York City firm that runs an advisory platform for tax and wealth practices. It operates three connected surfaces: a marketplace that matches individuals with complex financial situations (equity compensation, liquidity events, business owners, real estate, high net worth) to vetted tax advisors; a client portal and workflow platform that tax firms run their engagements, documents, questionnaires and e-file on; and Harness Wealth Advisers, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser that recommends third-party advisers. Harness publishes no public developer program — there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI or webhook documentation on any Harness host, and the product is delivered entirely as an end-user web application at app.harness.co.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Catalant
providers.description: Catalant is a consulting platform that connects organizations with a global marketplace of experienced independent consultants and boutique firms, positioning itself as "Consulting 2.0" fit-to-purpose consulting that is faster, more flexible, and more cost efficient than traditional large consulting firms. Its network spans 10,000+ vetted consultants (many from Fortune 500 companies and top-tier consulting firms, averaging 19+ years of experience) and serves 700+ businesses across 20+ countries. Catalant covers engagement areas including Digital & AI, Transformation & Value Creation, Operations, Sales & Marketing, M&A / Integration & Separation, Strategy & Finance, and Organization & People. Catalant is a General Catalyst portfolio company. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, and support properties.

providers.name: Harbor Global
providers.description: Harbor Global is a global professional-services firm delivering technology, operations, strategy, and intelligence consulting to law firms, corporate legal departments, and government legal teams. Its practice areas span legal-technology and operations (application management, process automation, AI enablement), strategic advisory, intelligence and research/library services, and vendor governance, delivered by a global team of specialists. Harbor has grown through acquisitions such as iTrain (UK legal-technology training and AI enablement) and CE Global Partners (HCM/HR and payroll transformation). It is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Harbor Global is a services company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company identity and discovery.

providers.name: LawTrades
providers.description: LawTrades is a legal talent marketplace, founded in 2016, that matches companies with vetted independent attorneys, paralegals, and legal operations professionals on flexible, on-demand terms rather than through traditional law firms or ALSPs. The platform covers eleven practice areas — commercial contracts, corporate law, data privacy and cyber security, intellectual property, labor and employment, legal operations, litigation, M&A, product counsel, real estate, and regulatory compliance — and handles matching, work-log management, invoicing, payments, and real-time spend analytics in-product. A human-in-the-loop AI layer drafts documents and flags risk for lawyer review. LawTrades raised a $6M Series A backed by 500 Global, Draper Associates, Social Capital, and AngelList. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Zehitomo
providers.description: Zehitomo is a Tokyo-based online marketplace that matches consumers in Japan with local professionals across hundreds of service categories — including photographers, personal trainers, house cleaners, graphic and web designers, videographers, tax accountants, interpreters, construction and repair trades, and business consultants. Clients describe the job they need done and receive quotes and proposals from vetted local pros, while professionals pay to respond to matched leads. Founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, Zehitomo runs a consumer-facing web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Slalom
providers.description: Slalom is a global business and technology consulting firm headquartered in Seattle, Washington, founded in 2001 and privately held, with roughly 12,000 employees across dozens of markets in North America, Europe, Asia and Australia. The firm delivers strategy, artificial intelligence, data, cloud and engineering, customer experience, legacy modernization, digital product building, and privacy and security consulting, and operates the Slalom Build brand for custom software, data platform and product engineering work. Slalom is a delivery partner for Microsoft, AWS, Salesforce, Google Cloud, Adobe and NVIDIA. It sells consulting engagements rather than software, and publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; the machine-readable surface it does publish is an llms.txt at its marketing root and a security.txt on the Slalom Build site.

providers.name: FTI Consulting
providers.description: FTI Consulting is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The FTI Consulting API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Robert Half International
providers.description: Robert Half International is the world's first and largest specialized staffing and talent solutions firm. Founded in 1948, it provides contract, temporary, and permanent placement solutions across finance and accounting, technology, marketing, legal, and administrative fields. The company is the parent of Protiviti, a global consulting firm. Robert Half does not publicly expose a developer API; integration is available through partner programs and ATS ecosystem connectors. Listed in the Fortune 500.

providers.name: EPAM Systems
providers.description: EPAM Systems is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The EPAM Systems API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Gerson Lehrman Group (GLG)
providers.description: Gerson Lehrman Group (GLG) is the world's leading platform for trusted human expertise, connecting organizations with a network of senior-level subject-matter experts to inform strategic decision-making. For more than 25 years GLG has facilitated expert calls and meetings, on-demand expert content and transcripts, quantitative and qualitative research and surveys, in-person and virtual events, and advisory and placement engagements. Its myGLG platform layers AI-powered and agentic research tools over that expert network. GLG was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. GLG operates no public developer API or documented developer program; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security surface.

providers.name: Alvarez & Marsal
providers.description: Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a leading global professional services firm, founded in 1983 by Tony Alvarez II and Bryan Marsal and headquartered in New York City. Privately held, the firm employs more than 10,000 people across six continents and is best known for turnaround and restructuring engagements (Lehman Brothers, HealthSouth, Tribune, FTX, Arthur Andersen) and for performance improvement, tax advisory, transaction advisory, disputes and investigations, valuation, and private equity performance improvement (PEPI) services. A&M does not operate a public developer portal; technology is delivered through client engagements, internal proprietary tools, A&M Capital Partners (the firm's investment arm), and a public Insights / thought-leadership surface published on alvarezandmarsal.com.

providers.name: Conduent
providers.description: Conduent is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Conduent API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Fractal Analytics
providers.description: Fractal Analytics Limited (fractal.ai) is an enterprise artificial intelligence services and products company founded in 2000, headquartered in New York with a large delivery footprint in India and roughly 5,000 employees across 18 global locations. Fractal sells AI consulting, data engineering, decision-science and design services to Fortune 500 clients in consumer packaged goods, retail, healthcare and life sciences, technology/media/telecom, financial services, insurance and industrials, and builds products on top of that practice — most notably Cogentiq, its enterprise agentic AI platform (with MCP and agent gateways, low-code agent builder and pre-built domain agents), LLM Studio, and consumer/vertical brands including Flyfish, Asper.ai, Kalaido.ai, Vaidya.ai and iqigai. The company listed on the NSE and BSE under the symbol FRACTAL in February 2026. Its API surface is delivered inside client engagements and gated product tenants rather than through a public developer program: as of this profiling pass Fractal publishes no public developer portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable API contract, and no hosted MCP server or A2A agent card.

providers.name: World 50 Group
providers.description: World 50 Group is an invitation-only membership community for CEOs, board directors, and C-suite executives from the world's largest and most respected companies. It runs highly curated peer communities organized by role (General Counsel 50, Procurement 50, Human Resource 50, President 50, Innovating 50, and more), the NEXT executive-development platform (Next Director, Next Leader, Next Generation Leadership), and publishes C-suite insights and impact research. Membership is by invitation; members access the community through the World 50 iOS/Android app. The company publishes no public developer program or API surface.

providers.name: Juno
providers.description: Juno (juno.co), operated by Juno Technology, Inc., is a San Francisco-based owner's representation, development-consulting and construction-management firm for prefabricated, modular and mass-timber multifamily development, working with developers from site feasibility and entitlement through delivery across North America. Juno owns the rights to the Juno Mass Timber System, a field-tested kit-of-parts building system of roughly 33 components configurable into 25+ unit types, proven on the 24-unit Juno East Austin project at 400 Comal St, Austin TX. The current company is the 2024 relaunch ("Juno 2.0") of the venture-funded Juno / Juno Residential founded in 2019 by Jonathan Scherr, BJ Siegel and Chester Chipperfield, which raised roughly $32M from Comcast Ventures, Khosla Ventures and RET Ventures before running out of money; the relaunched firm is led by co-founders Emily Mills Marineau and Jen Canchola. Juno sells professional services and a physical building system, not software: as of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site, a mass-timber system page, a contact form, a newsletter signup, terms of service and a privacy policy, and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Lexoo
providers.description: Lexoo is a commercial legal services provider that operates as an outsourced in-house legal team for businesses, concentrating on commercial contract review and negotiation. The company handles routine contract work at fixed rates per agreement with a stated maximum two-day turnaround, so internal legal and sales teams are freed for more strategic work. Alongside contract review, Lexoo runs multi-country projects that engage local counsel across more than 70 countries for work such as terms and conditions localisation and regulatory research, and it builds playbooks and training materials that let client teams handle standard agreements independently. The practice is led by Nathalie Lambert and serves scale-ups and start-ups, with published client references including Trustpilot, Nielsen, ComplyAdvantage, Xeneta, Chattermill and Jokr. Lexoo is not an API-first company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation or SDKs, and its only machine-readable surfaces are the standard WordPress REST API and RSS feed exposed by its marketing site.

providers.name: Maximus
providers.description: Maximus is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Maximus API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: CohnReznick
providers.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

providers.name: Cognizant Technology Solutions
providers.description: Cognizant Technology Solutions is a multinational information technology services and consulting company that provides digital, technology, consulting, and operations services to clients worldwide. Cognizant does not publish a general-purpose public REST API. Its developer-facing footprint is centered on the Cognizant Neuro AI platform family (Neuro AI Decisioning, Neuro AI Enterprise Core, Neuro AI Engineering, Neuro AI for IT Operations) and the open-source Neuro SAN multi-agent orchestration framework released by Cognizant AI Lab. Other delivered platforms (BigFrame for mainframe data migration, ADM accelerators, industry vertical solutions) are typically engaged via consulting engagements rather than self-service APIs.

providers.name: Lawhive
providers.description: Lawhive is a UK consumer legal-services marketplace that connects individuals and small businesses with regulated solicitors online at fixed, transparent prices, positioned as roughly half the cost of a traditional high-street law firm. Clients answer intake questions on the site, receive a quote or a callback, and are matched with a vetted consultant lawyer who then runs the matter end to end through the Lawhive platform, covering conveyancing, divorce and family, employment, immigration, landlord and tenant, and property work. Lawhive Ltd is not a law firm and does not give legal advice itself; regulated legal services are delivered by its network, including affiliate firm Lawhive Legal Ltd, which is authorised and regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA ID 8003766). The company is backed by Balderton Capital and GV. Lawhive publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation, so this profile captures its identity, legal and compliance posture, and probed domain-security surface rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Bain & Company
providers.description: Bain & Company is a global management consulting firm and one of the prestigious Big Three strategy consultancies. Bain does not publish a commercial public developer portal; technology integration is delivered through client-specific advisory engagements, Bain proprietary tools (NPS Prism, Helix, Vector), and a Bain-published Insights / research surface that is consumed via the bain.com website and feeds rather than developer APIs.

providers.name: Fox Rothschild LLP
providers.description: Fox Rothschild LLP is a national US law firm with approximately 1,000 attorneys across 30+ offices. The firm has no public developer APIs. Its programmatic surface is limited to publication and content distribution: subscription-based email alerts and 21+ topical attorney-authored blogs hosted on the LexBlog (WordPress) platform, each of which exposes a standard WordPress RSS 2.0 feed at /feed/. This index catalogs the firm and the RSS-able LexBlog network as the consumable surface.

providers.name: UL Solutions
providers.description: UL Solutions is a global leader in applied safety science, providing testing, inspection, certification, advisory, and software solutions to help customers innovate safely, demonstrate compliance, and bring trusted products to market. The company offers software products such as ULTRUS and ComplianceWire, customer portals (myUL, Product iQ), and the Marks and Labels Hub. UL Solutions does not currently expose a public developer-facing API portal with open documentation.

providers.name: Core10
providers.description: Core10, Inc. is a U.S.-based fintech software development and API integration firm founded in 2016 by Lee Farabaugh and Jeff Martin, headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee with delivery centers in Martin, Tennessee and Huntington, West Virginia, built on a domestic-outsourcing model it trademarked as Hereshore(R). Core10 wrote custom software, core-banking integrations and API layers for community banks, credit unions and fintechs, and acquired Accrue Technologies in 2021 to add a Salesforce-based digital lending, account opening and treasury onboarding platform. In January 2024 it spun its implementation practice out as Monarch, and the Core10 brand has since been retired: core10.io now 301-redirects to monarchfts.com, where Monarch operates as an Intapp DealCloud implementation, configuration and managed-services consultancy for private capital firms, while the Accrue platform trades independently at getaccrue.com under its own leadership. Core10 built API integrations for other companies for nearly a decade but never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract of its own, and as of 2026-08-11 neither successor brand does either.

providers.name: Crete Professionals Alliance
providers.description: Crete Professionals Alliance (rebranded in 2025 as "Current", current.co) is a growth platform for independent accounting firms, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The alliance provides member firms with technology, talent, capital, and strategy to compete at enterprise scale, spanning 48 partner firms across 39 states and 3 countries with more than 2,000 employees. Service lines include accounting, advisory, audit and attest, client accounting services, and tax. This is a professional services / accounting company, not a developer-facing API provider: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDKs, or technical documentation. The record is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph coverage of Bessemer holdings.

providers.name: EY
providers.description: One of the Big Four professional services firms providing audit, tax, consulting, and advisory services. Operates in over 150 countries helping businesses navigate regulatory and strategic challenges, and runs proprietary technology platforms such as EY Helix (analytics), EY Atlas (research), and EY Canvas (audit) for internal and engagement use.

providers.name: PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers)
providers.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms, with approximately 370,000 staff across a global network of member firms coordinated by PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited (PwCIL). PwC organizes delivery across three primary service lines — Assurance (audit), Tax (tax compliance, planning, and reporting), and Advisory (consulting, deals, and risk). The firm operates proprietary technology platforms including PwC Halo (a suite of data analytics tools used to support audit engagements), the Trusted AI initiative (PwC's responsible-AI governance and assurance framework), and ProEdge (a workforce upskilling platform). In April 2024 PwC announced a multi-year alliance with OpenAI positioning the firm as both OpenAI's largest customer and its first reseller of ChatGPT Enterprise, supporting PwC's broader generative-AI consulting practice. PwC's research and insights surface — pwc.com/insights, the annual Global CEO Survey, the Global Workforce Hopes and Fears Survey, the Money Tree report, and regional industry outlooks — is the firm's primary public-facing knowledge product. PwC does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, partner API documentation, or a GitHub organization at the corporate level. The github.com/pwc handle is held by an unrelated individual user (Patrick Clearwater). Any technical integrations with PwC platforms are arranged through engagement contracts and the PwC Technology Consulting practice rather than through self-service developer credentials. PwC's content distribution is reader-facing (newsletter subscriptions, the PwC US Newsroom, LinkedIn, YouTube) with no documented public RSS feed endpoint exposing news, press releases, or insights as a syndication contract.

providers.name: Aon
providers.description: Aon plc is a London-headquartered global professional services firm delivering integrated risk and human capital advisory through two reporting pillars — Risk Capital (broking, reinsurance, risk analytics) and Human Capital (health, wealth, talent, rewards). The firm operates in over 120 countries, lists on the NYSE under the ticker AON, and grew its US middle-market footprint with the April 2024 acquisition of NFP for roughly $13B. Aon publishes named analytics platforms (Risk Analyzer suite, ReMetrica, CyQu, Spectrum, Impact Forecasting catastrophe models, Radford McLagan Compensation Database, SkillsGraph, Gauge, Revenue GPS) but those tools are delivered through gated client portals — no developer portal, OpenAPI catalog, SDK org, or public API reference is published on aon.com.

providers.name: Mu Sigma
providers.description: Mu Sigma is a decision sciences and AI services company founded in 2004, headquartered in Northbrook, Illinois with its principal delivery centre in Bangalore, India, working with 140+ Fortune 500 clients across retail, pharma, financial services, manufacturing, energy, technology and logistics. Its work is delivered as engagements and platforms rather than as a public developer product: the Art of Problem Solving System (muAoPS), the Akashic Architecture enterprise intelligence foundation, the muTalos agentic-AI ecosystem, Enablers of Confidence, and a Continuous Service-as-a-Software operating model. Mu Sigma publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract; its only public machine-readable engineering output is a set of open-source R packages for decision science (HVT, muHVT, analysisPipelines, RImpala, Rdrools) released to CRAN from the github.com/Mu-Sigma organization.

providers.name: Korn Ferry
providers.description: Korn Ferry is a global organizational consulting firm that helps companies design optimal organization structures, recruit and develop talent, and drive performance. The firm offers services across executive search, leadership development, organizational strategy, total rewards, and talent acquisition. Korn Ferry serves clients across industries with a combination of consulting, data, and digital products.

providers.name: Concentrix
providers.description: Concentrix is a global technology and services leader providing customer experience (CX) management, digital transformation, and technology consulting across approximately 2,000 brands worldwide. Its product suite spans the iX product line (including iX Hello and iX Hero agentic AI assistants) and the Catalyst experience transformation and technology consultancy. Concentrix does not publish a public developer API; the iX product suite and Catalyst services are delivered via managed engagements and enterprise integrations rather than a self-service developer portal.

providers.name: Lab0
providers.description: Lab0 (lab0.ai) is a San Francisco company in the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch building an "AI forward-deployed engineer" for B2B SaaS: agentic systems that automate enterprise software implementation and post-sales delivery. The platform runs discovery, solution design, configuration, custom integration build, testing and go-live in parallel, with the stated goal of compressing 3-12 month deployment cycles down to weeks. Its connector agents profile a customer instance (tables, fields, auth model, processes) to produce a connector spec, then generate the integration, auth, field mappings, callbacks and write-back workflows as staged changes a human team reviews, with every write previewed as a controlled dry-run before it touches the customer instance. Named target systems are ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, Workday and Adobe AEM, plus custom APIs. As of this profile Lab0 is pre-launch as a developer platform: it publishes a marketing site and an llms.txt, but no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or self-serve sign-up. It is sold as a managed engagement via founder contact and demo booking.

providers.name: LegalPad
providers.description: Legalpad (Legalpad Inc, Seattle) was a startup-focused US work-visa and immigration company founded by Todd Heine and Sara Itucas, who first began processing visas together at Teleborder (Y Combinator 2013) and reunited in Techstars Seattle in 2017. Legalpad paired software with staff immigration attorneys to file O-1, H-1B, L-1, TN, E-1/E-2, E-3 and B-1 work visas plus EB-1A, EB-1B, EB-1C, EB-2 and EB-2 NIW employment-based green cards, and said it had helped 500+ companies at roughly one-third the typical processing time. It raised a $2M seed in 2018 and a $10M Series A in 2020 before being acquired by Deel in 2022, after which it operated as "Legalpad by Deel" inside Deel Immigration. The legalpad.io web presence was retired after 2024 and the business now lives on as Deel Immigration. Legalpad never published a public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK or other developer surface, so there is no API artifact to enrich.

providers.name: Foaster
providers.description: Foaster is an AI transformation consultancy that bills itself as "the AI-native McKinsey." Founded in 2026 by Raphael Dabadie and Alexandre Combes and backed by Y Combinator, it deploys AI agents that interview a company's employees at scale, map how work actually gets done, identify bottlenecks and AI opportunities, and draft a transformation roadmap in about two weeks, with expert consultants reviewing the outputs and feeding their corrections back into the system. Its offerings span an AI Transformation Assessment, Continuous AI Transformation with monthly adoption tracking, and Enterprise Deployment backed by forward-deployed engineers. Foaster is a managed professional-services company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other developer-facing technical surface.

providers.name: Lawdingo
providers.description: Lawdingo is a New York City legal-technology company founded in 2012 by Nikhil Nirmel and Dan Langevin, and a Y Combinator Winter 2013 alum backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst and AltaIR Capital. It launched as a consumer marketplace for talking to a lawyer on demand, then pivoted to serving law firms and corporate legal departments with remote paralegals and contract attorneys — legal research, litigation drafting, court filing and discovery support — delivered through an online platform where clients assign work, share documents, deposit funds and track hours. Lawdingo publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs, and as of this enrichment pass its lawdingo.com and www.lawdingo.com domains both return HTTP 404 "Site Not Found" from an unpublished Framer site, leaving no live web surface to harvest.

providers.name: McKinsey & Company
providers.description: McKinsey & Company is a global management consulting firm advising leading businesses, governments, non-profit organizations, and institutions on strategy, operations, technology, and transformation. The firm operates in more than 65 countries and runs QuantumBlack, its AI and analytics arm. No public developer portal or external APIs have been identified for McKinsey & Company; its proprietary platforms (e.g., platform.mckinsey.com) are gated to client engagements and authenticated users only.

providers.name: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI)
providers.description: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI) is a top-25 nationally ranked accounting and advisory firm headquartered in Alabama, operating 70+ locations across 13 states plus Mexico. The firm delivers audit and attest, tax, and advisory services (cybersecurity, fraud and forensics, valuations, and transaction advisory) to more than 18 industries, alongside value add-on subsidiaries including CRI Advanced Analytics, CRI CFO Hub, and CRI M&A Advisors, and is a member of PrimeGlobal. It was surfaced via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched here; note that criadv.com is a professional-services accounting firm, not a Bessemer-backed fintech startup, so the portfolio-lead tagging is a domain false-positive. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: Jacobs Engineering Group
providers.description: Jacobs Engineering Group, now operating as Jacobs Solutions, is one of the world's largest providers of professional, technical, and construction services, offering full-spectrum support to industries including aerospace, energy, environmental, infrastructure, and transportation. This entry is retained for legacy continuity; current activity is tracked under Jacobs Solutions.

providers.name: Kelly Services
providers.description: Kelly Services is a global leader in providing workforce solutions, connecting talented people to companies in need of their skills across a variety of industries including staffing, talent management, and outsourcing.

providers.name: ManpowerGroup
providers.description: ManpowerGroup is a global workforce solutions company that connects talented people with innovative companies through its family of brands including Manpower, Experis, and Talent Solutions. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: PwC
providers.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms providing audit and assurance, tax, and management consulting services globally. PwC operates as a network of member firms across approximately 150 countries with hundreds of thousands of professionals. Service lines include audit, deals and transactions, tax compliance and advisory, risk assurance, cybersecurity and privacy, ESG and sustainability assurance, workforce transformation, and digital/technology consulting (cloud, data, AI, ERP). PwC publishes thought-leadership content and operates client portals for engagement delivery and document exchange, but it does not publish a public developer API or open partner integration portal at the corporate level - client connectivity is bilateral and project-scoped rather than offered as a self-serve API product.

providers.name: Skillbridge
providers.description: Skillbridge (skillbridge.co) was a New York-based online marketplace for freelance consultants and independent professionals, connecting organizations from Fortune 500 companies to early-stage startups with vetted specialists for short-term engagements. Founded in 2013, it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. Skillbridge was acquired by Toptal in 2016 and folded into what became Toptal Business; the skillbridge.co domain now 301-redirects to toptal.com/finance. The company operates no independent developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface, so there are no technical artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: StarOfService
providers.description: StarOfService is an online local-services marketplace that connects consumers with vetted service professionals across home improvement, events, wellness, lessons, and business services. Headquartered in France and operating across multiple European markets, the platform matches customer project requests to nearby providers and facilitates quotes and messaging between them. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company exposes a consumer web marketplace and has no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Tallan
providers.description: Tallan was a Hartford, Connecticut technology consultancy, founded in 1985, that built custom Microsoft- and Azure-powered solutions — application modernization, e-commerce and web development, user experience, mobile, cloud, data, and AI/ML — for clients in manufacturing, consumer packaged goods, pharma, healthcare, and state and local government. In February 2023 Tallan was acquired by EY US and folded into EY's Microsoft services group; the tallan.com domain now 301-redirects to EY's Microsoft alliance page. Tallan operated as a professional-services consultancy and never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface, so there is no API to enrich.

providers.name: VisasQ
providers.description: VisasQ Inc. is a Tokyo-headquartered knowledge-sharing and spot-consulting platform that connects companies seeking specialized insight with a global network of roughly 800,000 experts across 190 countries and diverse industries and job functions. Its flagship "ビザスクdirect" service arranges one-on-one expert consultations, and it has launched "AI Scout" to deliver precision expert matches in under five minutes, 24/7. The company operates six global offices with multilingual support and over 600 employees, serving Japan and the United States as primary markets. VisasQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP surface; only domain-security posture could be probed.

providers.name: Blank Rome LLP
providers.description: Blank Rome LLP is an Am Law 100 U.S. law firm founded in 1946 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with approximately 600+ attorneys across roughly 14 U.S. offices plus an international presence (Shanghai). The firm provides comprehensive legal and government-advocacy services across commercial and corporate litigation, corporate / M&A and finance, restructuring and bankruptcy, government contracts, intellectual property, labor and employment, real estate, tax, white-collar defense, matrimonial and family law, and a nationally recognized maritime and international trade practice. Blank Rome Government Relations LLC, the firm's affiliated lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. The firm publishes practice-area client alerts, the Mainbrace maritime newsletter, and industry insights through its website's News & Events and Publications sections. Blank Rome does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization; this profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface (practice pages, newsletters, alerts) rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Jacobs Solutions
providers.description: Jacobs Solutions is a global technology-forward solutions company providing consulting, design, engineering, technical, scientific, and project delivery services for government and private sector clients across infrastructure, energy, environmental, advanced manufacturing, life sciences, and national security markets.

providers.name: Cozen O'Connor
providers.description: Cozen O'Connor is a full-service U.S. law firm founded in 1970 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with more than 1,000 attorneys across 33+ offices in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The firm is ranked among the top 100 law firms in America and is best known for its nationally recognized subrogation, insurance, labor and employment, global corporate, intellectual property, and government relations practices. Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies, the firm's bipartisan federal, state, and local government affairs and lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. and major state capitals. The firm operates an unusually broad thought-leadership network of LexBlog/WordPress-powered blogs and podcasts (subrogation, cyber law, health law, state AGs, transformative AI, OSHA, employment law, family law, property insurance, casualty coverage, real estate / land use, professional responsibility, and a Public Strategies feed), each of which exposes a standard `/feed/` RSS endpoint. Cozen O'Connor does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization. This profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface — practice and industry pages, attorney directory, ancillary businesses, lobbying arm, and the blog/podcast RSS network — rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Marsh & McLennan
providers.description: Marsh & McLennan Companies is a global professional services firm offering clients advice and solutions in risk, strategy, and people through Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer, and Oliver Wyman. providers.name: Service Corp International
providers.description: Service Corporation International is North America's leading provider of deathcare products and services, owning and operating funeral homes and cemeteries throughout the United States and Canada.
